final.title: The real limit of dual running
final.body:
Dual running looks harmless until you treat it as a real workflow decision. For a small business, it means keeping the manual process alive while a new AI-assisted path runs beside it. That only makes sense for one repeatable task where you are already weighing manual labour, another hire, or automation.

The limit is overlap. While both paths exist, someone has to check outputs, resolve differences, and decide which path is the source of truth. For money movement or other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. No shortcut there; the spreadsheet does not get a vote.

Bareni’s normal sequence is simple: identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, then define a small working MVP, a fixed scope, and clear measures. That is method, not a promise of results. The point of dual running is to learn whether the new path can carry the load before the old one is switched off.

A practical next step is to ask yourself: how much owner time goes into this workflow each week, and how many decision points genuinely need your judgment? If the answer is many, dual running may be too costly for long. If it is narrow, a short pilot can tell you whether the system is worth keeping.
